summary.title: Unpaid loans to a friend
summary.what_happened: Over the last year I have lent a friend about 900 euros in small amounts. Each time she said it was 'until payday'. She has paid back maybe 50 euros. When I mention the money, she changes the subject. She has posted photos from concerts and a weekend trip. I have never said no to her and I have never set a deadline for repayment.
summary.my_feelings: I'm starting to feel used by her.
summary.my_needs: I need to stop lending money without feeling guilty.
summary.desired_outcome: I want the money back, or at least a plan for repaying it.

consult.text:
It sounds like you are tired and a bit resentful. You have been generous for a year, and it is hard when the money does not come back and the subject gets changed. That is a reasonable thing to feel.

Your friend may see it differently. She may feel embarrassed about owing so much and avoid the topic because of that. Each loan was small, so she may not be tracking the total at all. The concerts and the trip may look to you like she has spare money, but we do not know what her finances or those costs really look like.

One thing that may have made this harder is that you have never said no or set a deadline. She may have taken the loans as fine because nothing told her otherwise. That does not excuse not repaying, but it is the part you can change.

What we do not know is whether she realises the total is about 900 euros.

Some next steps:
1. Tell her the total plainly and ask for a repayment plan with dates, even for small amounts.
2. Decide now what you will say to the next request, and say it kindly.
3. Work out what repayment you could accept, so you know what a good result looks like.
I feel bad, maybe I'm being greedy and should just let it go.

It makes sense that you feel bad. You care about her, and talking about money is uncomfortable. Wanting 900 euros back, or a plan, is a fair thing to want. Letting it go is also your choice to make.

I would keep one point in view. Because you have not set a limit or a deadline, she may not know this bothers you. Saying it clearly and kindly is the part that is in your hands.

Whichever way you decide, you can stop lending from now on. If you want the money back, you can do both.

Some steps:
1. Write down what you would be comfortable with: full repayment, part of it, or a plan.
2. Tell her the total and ask when she can start paying it back.
3. Prepare one calm sentence for the next request, such as "I can't lend money right now."

Then see how she responds before you decide what to do about the rest.

share_draft: Hi, I want to talk about something that has been on my mind. Over the last year I have lent you about 900 euros in small amounts, and I think you have paid back about 50. I haven't said anything before, and I never set a deadline, so that is partly on me. I have started to feel uncomfortable about it, and I don't want that to affect our friendship. I would like to agree on a plan for paying it back, even if it is small amounts. From now on I also need to stop lending money. How do you see it, and what would work for you?
